Hyperparameter selection

Data-driven hyperparameter selection

biodiversityDS .

Proper hyperparameter selection allows to develop model with higher potential for transferability.

# read occurrence records (presences) and transform to spatial object
library(terra)
presences <- read.table("../Data/Text delimited/species_presence_records.csv", sep = ";", header = TRUE)
presences <- vect(presences, geom = c("Lon", "Lat"))
S7 // Data-driven hyperparameter and monotonic constrains

biodiversityDS .
# download layers for present conditions
variables <- list(var1 = c("thetao", "mean", "depthmean"), var2 = c("o2", "mean", "depthmean"),
    var3 = c("phyc", "mean", "depthmean"))
environmentalLayers <- download_multiple_layers(variables = variables, experiment = c("baseline"),
    decade = c(2010))
# plot layers
plot(environmentalLayers, axes = TRUE)

S7 // Data-driven hyperparameter and monotonic constrains

biodiversityDS .
# develop a study region layer
myStudyRegion <- studyRegion(rasterLayers=environmentalLayers, # SpatRaster of layers
                             presences=presences, # presence records
                             distanceThreshold=200000, # distance from records in meters
                             topographyLayer = "../Data/Raster data/Bathymetry.tif", # bathymetry layer
                             verticalPref=c(-15,-300)) # known vertical distribution
# inspect the study region layer
plot(myStudyRegion, main="Study region", col="#979797", axes=TRUE)

S7 // Data-driven hyperparameter and monotonic constrains

biodiversityDS .
# crop the environmental layers to the extent of the study region
environmentalLayers <- crop(environmentalLayers, myStudyRegion)
# mask the environmental layers with the study region
environmentalLayers <- mask(environmentalLayers, myStudyRegion)
# plot the masked environmental layers
plot(environmentalLayers, axes = TRUE)

S7 // Data-driven hyperparameter and monotonic constrains

biodiversityDS .
# generate pseudo-absence and combine presences and background into a unique object
absences <- pseudoAbsences(rasterLayers = environmentalLayers, presences, n = 1000)
presences$PA <- 1
absences$PA <- 0
records <- rbind(absences, presences)
# extract environmental values and make an object with all information to model
modelData <- generateModelData(records, environmentalLayers, method = "blocks", bootstrapRounds = 10,
    sac = 50)
## Warning ::  190  records were removed because they have NA values in the environmental data

S7 // Data-driven hyperparameter and monotonic constrains

biodiversityDS .

To select the optimal hyperparameter, we can use a grid search approach. This is an approach that involves training models with different hyperparameter values and evaluating their performance in cross-validation.

# train the model with a set of hyperparameters
model <- trainModel(modelData, algorithm = "brt", hyperparameters = list(learning.rate = c(0.1,
    0.01, 0.001, 1e-04)))
# inspect the partial dependence plot of temperature effect
partialPlotOxygen <- partialPlot(model, modelData, variablePlot = "DissolvedMolecularOxygen_depthMean_Baseline_2010_mean")
partialPlotOxygen$partialPlot

# train the model with a set of hyperparameters
model <- trainModel(modelData, algorithm = "brt", hyperparameters = hyperparametersList)

S7 // Data-driven hyperparameter and monotonic constrains

Monotonicity

Monotonicity constrains in species distribution modelling

biodiversityDS .

Monotonicity constrains are used to ensure that the predicted response of a model is monotonic with respect to a given predictor variable. This means that the predicted response should either increase or decrease as the value of the predictor variable increases, but not both. This approach can force responses to meet ecological expectations.

# inspect the name of layers
names(environmentalLayers)
## [1] "OceanTemperature_depthMean_Baseline_2010_mean"        
## [2] "DissolvedMolecularOxygen_depthMean_Baseline_2010_mean"
## [3] "TotalPhytoplankton_depthMean_Baseline_2010_mean"
# monotonic constrains
monoton <- c("OceanTemperature_depthMean_Baseline_2010_mean"=-1, # negative effect
             "DissolvedMolecularOxygen_depthMean_Baseline_2010_mean"=1, # positive effect
             "TotalPhytoplankton_depthMean_Baseline_2010_mean"=1) # negative effect
# train the model
model <- trainModel(modelData, algorithm ="brt", monotonicity=monoton)
S7 // Data-driven hyperparameter and monotonic constrains

biodiversityDS .
# inspect the partial dependence plot of temperature effect
partialPlotTemperature <- partialPlot(model, modelData, variablePlot = "OceanTemperature_depthMean_Baseline_2010_mean")
partialPlotTemperature$partialPlot
